visual.general_description: Flowchart of a stepwise diagnostic and management pathway for neonates with persistent urticarial rash and systemic inflammation.
visual.detailed_description: Flowchart with a blue top box "Neonatl with persistent urticarial rash with systemic inflammation" (spelled as printed). Below it, a gray box "Initial stabilization Empirical antimicrobial therapy" leads to a gray decision box "Response to empirical therapy ?". The "Yes" branch goes left to a blue box "Continue: manage as suspected infection". The "NO" branch goes down to a yellow box "Comprehensive work-up" listing "1.Infectious disease (advanced cultures, PCR ) e.g. TORCH", "2.immune-mediated autoantibodies e.g. Neonatal Lupus" and "3.Hematologic ferritin,figrinogen, sCD25 e.g. HLH" (spelled as printed). That leads to a gray decision box "alternative diagnosis confirmed": "Yes" goes to a blue box "Institute specific therapy" and "NO" goes to an orange box "Assess for “Red Flags” for autoinflammatory Disease". An arrow rises from the orange box to a yellow decision box "High clinical suspicion for autoinflammatory disease ?" at the upper middle. Its "NO" branch goes right to a gray box "Continue monitoring and re-evaluation"; its "Yes" branch goes down to a blue box "Genetic testing e.g. whole exome sequencing", then to a gray decision box "Pathogenic variant identified ?". "NO" leads right to a gray box "Consider somatic mosaicism or repeat/expanded genetic analysis" and "Yes" leads down to a blue box "Initiate targeted biologic therapy e.g. IL-1 blockade". A dotted-outline text box at lower right begins "This flowchart outlines a stepwise approach to the evaluation and management of a neonate with a persistent urticarial rash and signs of systemic inflammation" and gives a key to "Red Flag" clinical features: Rash, CNS Involvement, Musculoskeletal, Inflammatory Markers and Fever Pattern, each with a short definition.
